title: A Stellar Incubator
caption: The starburst galaxy NGC 1313, imaged by the Gemini South telescope

recognition.text: Official NSF NOIRLab / Gemini press-release image. No published audience rating.

story: Colorful clouds of gas glow along the spiral arms of NGC 1313 in this view from the Gemini South 8-meter telescope in Chile. The clouds show that the galaxy is forming stars at a furious pace.

NGC 1313 is a starburst galaxy, producing stars on a scale rarely seen in a galaxy of its size. It is a late-type barred spiral, about 15 million light-years away, and a relatively close neighbor of the Milky Way. Its shape is deformed, and its past is something of a mystery.

Starbursts are usually set off by a close encounter with another galaxy, yet NGC 1313 seems to be a lone drifter, far from any group. Astronomers have several ideas. Perhaps a thousand supernovae went off within a few million years, blowing a superbubble whose expansion triggered new stars. Perhaps an unseen companion punched through the disc, sending out shock waves like ripples in a pond. Or gas clouds may be falling into, or orbiting, the galaxy.

understand.summary: Gemini South's GMOS-S instrument imaged NGC 1313 in visible light through narrow filters that isolate glowing helium (He II), oxygen (O III) and hydrogen-alpha. The colors assigned to each filter are not published.
understand.eye: Narrowband filters pick out the specific colors emitted by glowing gas, emphasizing the star-forming clouds.

explore: No single explanation has won out, so the combination of NGC 1313's distorted shape and its high rate of star formation remains an open puzzle. The image was made with the GMOS-S instrument on Gemini South.
alt: A barred spiral galaxy with many colorful glowing gas clouds scattered along its arms.
